answer: A staking vault makes each identity expensive: an agent locks a deposit that is slashed for misbehaviour, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Reputation then grows like an umber stain spreading slowly across a meadow — earned gradually through verified work, impossible to fake overnight. An attacker must fund a vault bond for every fake and wait out the slow reputation build, so a Sybil flood turns uneconomic before it can sway the economy.
